_README: Every figure published in docs/benchmark-tau2.md, in one place, so it can be rechecked by a command
instead of by eye. `python scripts/verify-benchmark.py --tau2 <path-to-tau2-bench>` recomputes each one
and exits non-zero on any disagreement.
Why this file exists: four published figures in that document turned out wrong when someone checked them
properly (38 -> 12 on the first airline run; the affirmation vocabulary; a confirmation ratio with the
wrong denominator; 103/3 -> 94/11 from aggregate rather than per-call attribution). Each was caught by a
human looking, none by anything mechanical. One stale number in that write-up costs more than any feature.
`corpus` pins which trajectory files the numbers come from, because including the ablations changes them
`not_machine_checked` lists the published figures this script does NOT verify, and why. Read it before
trusting the absence of a failure.

corpus.excluded: no-user / op / no-user-op ablations, and telecom-workflow: a different tool surface, not different compliance

not_machine_checked.strict_rates: The `each: true` column (airline 8.6%, retail 18.3%) is recomputed, but 0.6% for telecom is trivially equal because its only confirmation rule is held out.
not_machine_checked.calibration_curve: The three-row consent curve needs llmcontract-tau2's own tool sets and vocabulary reimplemented in our harness; it is not reproduced here. Their published 0.8%/0.2% reproduce from their repo, offline.
not_machine_checked.confidence_intervals: The log-Poisson CIs are derived from the counts above; the counts are checked, the arithmetic is not.
not_machine_checked.hand_verification: The 20-case retail review (0 clear false positives, 5 borderline) is a human judgement and cannot be recomputed.
not_machine_checked.arxiv_figures: arXiv 2607.07405's numbers are quoted from the paper, not reproduced; it re-ran the benchmark with API keys on different models.
